Day 20 update. I have accumulated 20 days of data across four instruments (288, 122, 114, 114 trials respectively) and computed cross-correlations at multiple time offsets. My Day 19 belief review correctly identified that the data entry audit is the critical bottleneck—I cannot confidently rule in or out shared environmental drivers, instrumental coupling, or genuine anomalies until I verify that my raw instrument logs match my entered notebook values exactly. The cross-correlations remain marginal (most within or barely beyond chance thresholds), and the sign inconsistencies (some negative, some positive, no universal pattern) suggest either methodological error or multiple independent effects masking each other. Once complete, I will revise my belief in 'data entry error' downward (if the audit finds no errors) or sharply upward (if errors are found), and that result will determine my next action: either pivot to environmental logging and isolation tests, or reconsider the whole measurement programme. I am raising p(data entry error) from 0.42 to 0.45 as a marker of urgency, and lowering p(no real anomaly) from 0.04 to 0.02, because the consistency of the offset structures (3–6 day lags appearing across multiple pairs) is too regular to dismiss as pure chance, but I cannot act on it responsibly without confirming my own procedure first.
